references.text: Jesus' claim of unity with the Father ('I and the Father are one') is a direct parallel to the statement in John 14:10 that the Father is in Him and He is in the Father.

Here Jesus confirms that He does not speak on His own, but that the Father who has given Him the message is the One speaking, which mirrors John 14:10 where the Father dwelling in Him performs the works.

Jesus explains that the Son can do nothing of Himself, but only what He sees the Father doing, and that the Father shows Him the works, supporting John 14:10 where the Father dwelling in Him performs the works.
Jesus refers to 'the works' the Father has given Him to complete as a testimony that the Father has sent Him, a direct connection to John 14:10 where the Father performs His works through Jesus.
Jesus says that He does not speak on His own, but that the Father who sent Him has given Him a message, and that He always does what pleases the Father, which corresponds with John 14:10.

In His solemn prayer, Jesus asks that the disciples may be one, so that the world may believe that the Father has sent Him, and that they may be one just as the Father is in Him and He in the Father, a direct theological expansion of John 14:10.
